title: AI Campaign Production
description: A lightweight control layer for AI-assisted campaign assembly across Jira, CMS and DAM, with human attention focused on exceptions and consequential decisions.
reviewQuestions: Does the Attention → Campaigns → Actions / Manifest model make the workflow legible without recreating CMS or DAM?
Are intervention states and automated readiness states visually distinct enough?
Can reviewers understand what automation assembled, what still needs a human, and where to go next?

versions.name: Stable V0 handoff
versions.whatChanged: Established the accepted information architecture: global Attention and Campaigns, with campaign-level Actions and Manifest, plus a stable master-detail shell.
versions.question: Can a lightweight control layer coordinate campaign assembly while keeping exceptions, provenance and human checkpoints visible?
versions.decisionRationale: Selected as the accepted baseline for controlled hardening in Cursor. New explorations should branch from this baseline rather than overwrite it.

decisionLog.decision: Use Attention and Campaigns as the two top-level views, with Actions and Manifest inside a selected campaign.
decisionLog.rationale: This separates operational follow-up from campaign status and avoids rebuilding CMS/DAM navigation inside the control layer.

decisionLog.decision: Treat CMS and DAM as systems of record.
decisionLog.rationale: Campaign Production should explain state, surface exceptions and route the user to detailed production work rather than duplicate existing editing surfaces.

decisionLog.decision: Protect the accepted baseline during exploration.
decisionLog.rationale: The V0 phase showed that broad rewrites could regress already accepted screens. New alternatives must preserve the current version until deliberately promoted.

decisionLog.decision: Do not use Overview / Content / Assets as campaign tabs.
decisionLog.rationale: That structure made the control layer feel like another CMS/DAM browser rather than a workflow-oriented production surface.

context.problem: Campaign production spans source tickets, structured CMS content and DAM assets. Mechanical assembly can be automated, but users still need a clear view of progress, exceptions and consequential decisions.
context.intendedOutcome: Produce a credible first draft of a campaign automatically while keeping human attention focused on unresolved or uncertain work and preserving direct paths into the systems of record.
context.workflow: A source ticket triggers campaign interpretation, asset and content discovery, CMS/DAM assembly and readiness checks. Campaign Production then surfaces unresolved actions and a read-only manifest of what was assembled.
context.currentDirection: A restrained enterprise control layer: Attention shows cross-campaign work that needs a human; Campaigns shows status; Actions shows what must happen next; Manifest shows what automation created and where it lives.
constraints: Do not become another CMS or DAM.
Do not hide consequential automation or unresolved exceptions.
Use shared underlying state for global Attention and campaign Actions.
Preserve accepted screens when testing a new exploration.
Keep detailed content and asset editing in the systems of record.
acceptedDecisions: Attention and Campaigns are the top-level information architecture.
Actions and Manifest are the selected-campaign views.
Folders appear before Content and Assets in Manifest.
Campaign lifecycle status is distinct from object readiness status.
Signed-off campaigns can be duplicated; all non-archived campaigns can be archived.
openQuestions: What is the clearest final treatment for semantic status messages in Attention, Actions and Manifest?
How should external CMS/DAM state changes be simulated in the portfolio prototype without implying false integration?
Which additional candidate explorations are worth preserving once Cursor hardening begins?
